title: WHO guideline (L1)
description: An L1 publication containing recommendations for clinical practice or public health policy, structured as the WHO Handbook for Guideline Development (2nd ed.) §12.1 "Guideline format" requires, with the SMART additions Mehl 2021 names: uniquely identified recommendations and data recommendations. Sections modelled by smart-kg L1 classes are the ones a smart-kg L1 graph of the guideline holds (bean 8pzh).

sections.title: Executive summary
sections.description: A stand-alone summary that states the key recommendations, each with its strength and the certainty of its evidence.

sources.note: All guidelines should have an executive summary, a main body and appendices. The executive summary should contain the key recommendations of the guideline.
the strength of the recommendation and the quality of the evidence for each recommendation should be specified in the executive summary

sections.title: Table of contents
sections.description: Navigational listing of the main-body sections.

sources.note: The main text of the guideline should include a table of contents, introduction, methods, recommendations and conclusions.

sections.title: Target audience and persons affected
sections.description: Who will apply the recommendations (end-users), distinguished from the people who receive the interventions.

sources.locator: §2.2.3 Who is the target audience?, PDF p.29; sections/sec-030-223-who-is-the-target-audience.md
sources.note: Guidelines must have a clearly defined target audience (end-user) which is identified early in the guideline development process

sources.locator: §2.2.3 Who is the target audience?, PDF p.29; sections/sec-030-223-who-is-the-target-audience.md

sections.title: Declarations of interest and their management
sections.description: Lists every participant with role and affiliation, and summarises how declarations of interest were collected, assessed and managed (stating explicitly if none were disclosed); acknowledges peer reviewers.

sources.note: All participants, roles and affiliations should be listed, with their conflicts of interests and how these were managed.

sources.locator: §6.11 Reporting declarations of interest in the guideline, PDF pp.84-86; sections/sec-105-6102-minimizing-the-risk-posed-by-conflicts-of-i.md
sources.note: A summary of how declarations of interest were collected, assessed and managed must be included in the main guideline document.
The GRC will not approve a guideline document that does not contain this information.
a copy of the published guideline (which includes an acknowledgement of their contribution)
L1 also recognises the need for increased representation of health informaticians on guideline panels

sections.title: Funding sources
sections.description: Names every funder of the guideline and, where not evident, the type of entity.

sources.locator: §6.8 Table 6.2 Principles for declarations of interest, PDF pp.76-79; sections/sec-099-68-assessing-declarations-of-interests.md
sources.note: All funding sources should be reported in the planning proposal and in the final guideline.

sources.locator: §3.6 Funders of the guideline, PDF p.46; sections/sec-060-36-funders-of-the-guideline.md
sources.note: The funder(s) of a guideline can play no role in the guideline development process and should not influence the recommendations.

sections.title: Key questions (PICO) and outcomes
sections.description: The foreground questions in population-intervention-comparator-outcome form, the outcomes rated important or critical, and optionally an analytic framework. The PICO question sets themselves come from the guideline development group's scoping and the systematic reviews behind it, which smart-base has not ingested. So this section names no `computedFrom`: computing it needs an evidence graph that does not exist yet (owner, 2026-10-04, bean qvxh, option 1). Ingesting that evidence is bean folio-assistant-0lde.

sources.note: Recommendations need to be clear and actionable, reflect the PICO format
The analytic framework may be included with the planning proposal or in the final guideline publication
10.2 Foreground (key/PICO) questions

sections.title: Evidence retrieval and synthesis
sections.description: Search strategy, study selection and synthesis of the systematic reviews informing each key question; full reviews may sit in annexes. The systematic reviews it summarises (for WHO guidelines, typically Cochrane or WHO-commissioned reviews) are external evidence that smart-base has not ingested. So this section names no `computedFrom`: computing it needs an evidence graph that does not exist yet (owner, 2026-10-04, bean qvxh, option 1). Ingesting that evidence is bean folio-assistant-0lde.

sources.note: The systematic reviews need to be reported in compliance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)

sources.note: The development and finalization of the strategies for searching for evidence that meets the established inclusion criteria is a fundamental step

sections.title: Certainty of the evidence (GRADE)
sections.description: GRADE assessment of the body of evidence per outcome and key question, summarised in evidence profiles. The GRADE evidence profiles it summarises are built from external systematic reviews (typically Cochrane) that smart-base has not ingested. So this section names no `computedFrom`: computing it needs an evidence graph that does not exist yet (owner, 2026-10-04, bean qvxh, option 1). Ingesting that evidence is bean folio-assistant-0lde.

sources.locator: §9.2 What are GRADE evidence profiles?, PDF p.122; sections/sec-154-92-what-are-grade-evidence-profiles.md
sources.note: GRADE evidence profiles contain the assessment of the quality of the evidence and a summary of findings across studies
GRADE evidence profiles, evidence-to-decision frameworks and tables, and any other relevant documentation can be supplied in appendices

sections.title: Evidence to decision
sections.description: Records the judgements on benefits and harms, values and preferences, resources, equity, acceptability and feasibility that shaped each recommendation's direction and strength. Its judgements rest on the GRADE evidence profiles and the systematic reviews behind them, which smart-base has not ingested. So this section names no `computedFrom`: computing it needs an evidence graph that does not exist yet (owner, 2026-10-04, bean qvxh, option 1). Ingesting that evidence is bean folio-assistant-0lde.

sources.note: These tables enhance the transparency of the process, focus the discussions of the GDG and permit recording of the judgements made
the GDG should, at a minimum, document its judgements on the four main factors.

sections.title: Recommendations
sections.description: Each recommendation stated actionably, with its direction, strength, certainty of evidence, justification and remarks on applicability, linked to its evidence. For SMART use, each is uniquely identified so digital systems can cite it, and data recommendations may be included.

sources.note: The main text of the guideline should include a table of contents, introduction, methods, recommendations and conclusions.
contain an indication of their strength and of the quality of the evidence on which they are based.
A recommendation should include a justification as to why it is strong or conditional and why it is for or against a given intervention.
Each recommendation should be linked to a summary of the evidence
uniquely identifying recommendations, which are updated as evidence improves over time (living guidelines)
L1: Narrative Guideline and data recommendations: Enhanced guidelines

sections.title: Implementation and adaptation considerations
sections.description: Conditions, context, acceptability concerns and adaptation points relevant to applying the recommendations in a setting.

sources.note: contain a set of remarks explaining the conditions and context in which the recommendation applies and the points to bear in mind regarding implementation.
a strategy to address concerns about acceptability during implementation will be included in the guideline with the recommendations.

sources.locator: Ch.13 Adaptation, implementation and evaluation, PDF pp.177-178; sections/sec-246-13-adaptation-implementation-and-evaluation.md
sources.note: Although implementation and evaluation plans do not need to be described in the guideline, they should be considered by the steering group
The adaptation toolkit and monitoring framework aim to facilitate country adaptation and implementation of the recommendations.

sections.title: Equity, human rights and gender considerations
sections.description: How the recommendations bear on equity, human rights, gender and social determinants, and how their equity impact should be evaluated.

sources.locator: §5.4.3.1 Producing and publishing the guideline, PDF pp.65-66; sections/sec-089-543-phase-3-publishing-and-updating.md
sources.note: The final guideline and in its derivative products must convey clear messages with respect to equity, human rights, gender and social determinants.
Evaluation and monitoring of the impact of recommendations that potentially affect inequities are also critically important and should be articulated in the guideline document.

sections.title: Monitoring and evaluation
sections.description: Outcome or performance measures that can be monitored for the main recommendations.

sources.note: The guideline should include outcome or performance measures that can be monitored for the main recommendations.
WHO recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience,6 as well as the adaptation toolkit7 and monitoring framework8 are illustrative tools of ANC L1.

sections.title: Research gaps and future research
sections.description: Knowledge gaps that leave the balance of benefits and harms uncertain, with suggested questions (ideally in PICO form) and methods to close them.

sources.note: such knowledge gaps should be described and questions and methods for addressing the gaps should be suggested.
This section of the guideline document will inform future recommendations and guidelines.
the guideline should outline the key gaps in knowledge and provide an agenda for future research.

sections.title: Conclusions
sections.description: Closing summary of the main body.

sections.title: Validity and updating
sections.description: The review-by date and how the recommendations will be kept current; under SMART, recommendations are versioned as living guidance.

sources.note: WHO guidelines should be issued with a “review-by” date to indicate how long the recommendations are expected to remain valid.
